subject: Post-call: Function calls & deterministic outputs -- AcmePay discovery recap
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmepay.com>, Megan Lee <megan.lee@acmepay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Function calls & deterministic outputs -- AcmePay discovery recap

Thanks again for the call earlier, Alex and Megan — good discussion. Below is a concise recap (pain, goal, current stack, and clear next steps) so we have alignment before we draft a POC scope. I’ve attached a first-pass schema stub for the tool/function handshake and a short POC scope spreadsheet.

Pain and priority (what we heard)
- Fraud/risk ops currently running batch reranks with high latency for edge cases; they need deterministic structured outputs for downstream automation.
- Manual post-processing of model text is adding ~3 FTEs of rule-based cleanup.
- Compliance requires auditable inputs/outputs and stable formatting for downstream parsers.

Goals (what success looks like for AcmePay)
- Deterministic tool outputs: JSON schema validated, no free-form deviations for critical fields (transaction_id, verdict, confidence_score).
- <50ms added latency over baseline for the tool-call path in 95th percentile (production target later).
- Integration: easiest path is via function-call interface (server receives schema-constrained payload, agent executes lookup + model call, returns validated JSON).

Current stack (as stated on the call)
- Core stack: Java backend + Kafka, risk microservice in Python, Postgres for events.
- No existing LLM infrastructure; plan is to host inference with Redwood Dedicated or Private (they prefer VPC).
- Security: SOC2 + SSO in place; they will require access controls and audit logs for the POC.

Key technical constraints
- Outputs must be schema-validated (we discussed JSON Schema v7 or equivalent).
- Agent workflow must support deterministic steps: pre-check -> model call -> post-validate -> event emit.
- KV/state caching for context to avoid re-hydrating user transaction history on every request.

Redwood proposal input (what we offered on the call)
- Provide a sample function-call schema (attached: acmepay_tool_call_schema_v1.json) that maps to their risk fields.
- POC scope: 2-week sandbox (integration + 10k events/day simulated load) and an evaluation harness to measure deterministic compliance and latency.
- Deliverables: schema, small adapter (Python) that demonstrates the function-call handshake, and a short runbook showing failure modes and fallback behavior.

Immediate next steps (owners & timelines)
- AcmePay: confirm success criteria and list of 3 canonical transaction types to validate (Alex) — due Wed 2026-06-17.
- Redwood: produce POC SOW + cost estimate and POC checklist (Olga) — will send by Tue 2026-06-16 EOD.
- Tech deep dive session to map schema to their risk fields (redwood infra + AcmePay risk lead) — propose Wed 6/18 10:00 PT.

Attachments (stubs)
- acmepay_tool_call_schema_v1.json (schema stub; fields: transaction_id, verdict, confidence_score, resolution_reasons[])
- acmepay_poc_scope.xlsx (POC milestones + telemetry matrix)

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the SOW and a proposed time for the deep dive.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0129

Subject: Re: Post-call: Function calls & deterministic outputs -- AcmePay discovery recap

Thanks, Olga — this matches our notes. A couple quick clarifications: 
- The three transaction types we want to validate for the POC are: chargebacks, disputed payouts, and suspicious login-linked transactions. We’ll produce sample datasets for each.
- For determinism: we need a strict schema for the POC (happy to lock fields) — the JSON stub is a good start.
- On latency: 95th percentile target is realistic; we also want a separate metric for end-to-end from Kafka read -> event emit.

Please include costs for both Dedicated (short-term) and Private (if we move to VPC).

Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Risk Engineering, AcmePay

Ack — I’ll draft the SOW this morning. Early checklist for the POC (first pass):
- SOW: scope, milestones, acceptance criteria (schema conformance, 95th pctl latency target, audit log sampling).
- Infra: Dedicated vs Private pricing + network egress assumptions.
- POC infra tasks: deploy sandbox VPC, provision GPU pool (min 1 node), pre-warm KV cache for typical transaction contexts.
- Deliverables: adapter + sample harness (kafka producer -> adapter -> function-call -> validator -> kafka emitter).
- Telemetry: token-level cost, per-request latency histogram, schema validation pass rate.

Attachments:
- acmepay_poc_scope.xlsx (POC timeline & telemetry matrix)

I’ll share a draft SOW with line-items for committed capacity and an optional Private deployment add-on.
